title: Phoenix theophrasti
wikitext: {{Short description|Species of palm}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2024}} {{Speciesbox |image = Phoenix theophrasti B.jpg |image_caption = Cretan date palm at the beach in Vai, Crete |status = LR/nt |status_system = IUCN2.3 |status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Johnson, D. |date=1998 |title=''Phoenix theophrasti'' |volume=1998 |article-number=e.T38630A10140653 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.1998.RLTS.T38630A10140653.en}} |genus = Phoenix |species = theophrasti |authority = [[Werner Rodolfo Greuter|Greuter]] |range_map = Phoenix theophrasti range.svg |range_map_caption = ⏺ Isolated native population }} '''''Phoenix theophrasti''''', the '''Cretan date palm''', is a [[Arecaceae|palm]] native to the eastern [[Mediterranean]], in the southernmost points of [[Greece]] and [[Turkey]]. It, along with ''[[Chamaerops humilis]]'' (the European fan palm) are the only native palm species in the Mediterranean basin; areas forested with these species constitute Europe's only palm [[forest]]s.{{cite book |author1=Johnson, D.V. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IPr7U0Cv3uwC |title=Palms: Their Conservation and Sustained Utilization: Status Survey and Conservation Action Plan |author2=Group, I.S.P.S. |publisher=IUCN |year=1996 |isbn=978-2-8317-0352-7}} Similarly in Turkey, it is the only native palm species; all other species—although much more common—are introduced. == Taxonomy == The [[botanical name|specific epithet]] ''theophrasti'' was chosen by the Swiss botanist [[Werner Greuter]] in 1967 from the fact that [[Theophrastus]], the ancient Greek "father of botany", had described several types of palms, including one from [[Crete]].{{cite journal|last=Hazir|first=A.|author2=H. D. Buyukozturk|title=''Phoenix'' spp. and other ornamental palms in Turkey: The threat from red palm weevil and red palm scale insects|journal=Emirates Journal of Food and Agriculture|year=2013|volume=25|issue=11|page=843|doi=10.9755/ejfa.v25i11.16500|doi-access=free}} A genomic study from New York University Abu Dhabi Center for Genomics and Systems Biology showed that domesticated [[date palm]] (''Phoenix dactylifera'') varieties from [[North Africa]], including well-known varieties such as Medjool and Deglet Noor, are a hybrid between Middle East date palms and ''P. theophrasti''.{{cite journal|last=Flowers|first=Jonathan|display-authors=etal|title=Cross-species hybridization and the origin of North African date palms|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA]]|year=2019|volume=116|issue=5|pages=1651–1658|doi=10.1073/pnas.1817453116|pmid=30642962|pmc=6358688|doi-access=free|bibcode=2019PNAS..116.1651F }} ==Description== Apart from the usually inedible dates and upright fruit clusters, the Cretan species can appear quite similar to the cultivated date. ''Phoenix theophrasti'' grows up to {{Convert abbreviated|15|m}} tall, usually with several slender stems. The [[leaf|leaves]] are pinnate, {{Convert abbreviated|2-3|m|ft}} long, with numerous rigid greyish-green linear leaflets {{Convert abbreviated|15-50|cm|sigfig=1}} long on each side of the central rachis. Dead leaves are [[marcescent]], remaining attached to the stem for years after withering. The [[fruit]] is an oval yellowish-brown [[drupe]] {{Convert abbreviated|1.5|cm|sigfig=1}} long and {{Convert abbreviated|1|cm|sigfig=1}} diameter and containing a single large [[seed]]. The fruit pulp is too thin and fibrous to be of agricultural significance and has an acrid taste, though the fruits are sometimes eaten by the locals. ==Distribution== The species has a relatively restricted distribution, mostly confined to southern Greece (a few sites on Crete and nearby islands), as well as some places on the Turkish coast. === Greece === Sites on Crete include [[Vai (Crete)|Vai]] in the [[Lasithi]] Prefecture, Ayios Nikitas in [[Heraklion]] Prefecture, and [[Preveli]] gorge and Souda near Plakias, both on the south coasts of [[Crete]] in [[Rethymnon]] Prefecture. Trees are also found on [[Amorgos]] island, on [[Halki (Greece)|Halki]] Island,{{Cite journal|last=Vernicos|first=Nicolas|title=Chalki in the Dodecanese|url=https://www.academia.edu/26689265|language=en}} and on the south coast of [[Anafi]] island. Recently, around 10 trees, the only natural stand on the mainland, were found in an ancient palm forest in the [[Epidaurus]] area in [[Peloponnese]].{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} It has been proposed that its range was much more widespread in [[Ancient Greece]], growing from [[Crete]] to [[Ancient Thebes (Boeotia)|Thebes]] and from the [[Peloponnese]] to [[Delos]].{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} === Turkey === Its presence in Turkey was not described scientifically until the 1980s. There are four stands in southwest Turkey,{{cite web|url=http://www.arkive.org/species/GES/plants_and_algae/Phoenix_theophrasti|title=''Phoenix theophrasti''|publisher=[[ARKive]]|access-date=18 May 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060630063919/http://www.arkive.org/species/GES/plants_and_algae/Phoenix_theophrasti/|archive-date=30 June 2006}} especially on the [[Datça]] and [[Bodrum]] Peninsulas in [[Muğla Province]] and in [[Kumluca]]-Karaöz in Finike Bay. The plants form a grove in the village of Gölköy in northern Bodrum are considered by some as a subspecies, having a shorter stem (4–8 m) but longer fruit stalks (0.6–2 m).{{cite journal|last=Boydak|first=Melih|author2=Sasha Barrow|title=A New Locality for Phoenix in Turkey: Gölköy-Bödrum|journal=[[Principes (botany)|Principes]]|year=1995|volume=39|issue=3|pages=117–122|url=http://www.palms.org/principes/1995/vol39n3p117-122.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826162828/http://www.palms.org/principes/1995/vol39n3p117-122.pdf |archive-date=26 August 2012 }} ==References and external links== {{Commons}} {{Reflist}} *Davis, P.
